newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares climb, following Wall Street's rise.
newsitem.headline: German shares climb, following Wall Street's rise.

text.p: German shares kicked off the week on a stronger than expected note, darting over two percent higher in early Monday bourse trade, as dealers attempt to catch up with Wall Street's firm close last Friday.
Shortly after the opening bell, Germany's blue-chip DAX index was trading up 2.27 percent, or 73.66 points higher at 3,318.59 points.
"What we are seeing is the typical short-squeeze," said one trader, adding however that the gains might soon fall victim to profit-taking.

Wall Street ended the session up 48.72 points at 6,526.07, successfully shaking off an earlier beating inflicted by jobs data. Dealers said the market was ignoring the suggestions of inflationary pressures presented by the unemployment report.
Speaking of considerable nervousness in the markets, dealers predicted the DAX index could fall back to 3,250 today.
Much will however depend on what happens once Wall Street opens, dealers said.
Chemical group BASF AG, still benefitting from an upbeat outlook for the current year, was the day's most heavily traded issue, rising 2.25 marks to 65.90 marks.
BASF's rivals Bayer AG and Hoechst AG were also faring well.
